facts:
## CELL FACTS

Cell 水_正官 (Water carrying The Magistrate). Persona The Magistrate (正官). Definition line: "Framework-mediated pressure, the standard that steadies". Keyword Order, charge gentle, poles catalyst Integrity / friction Rigidity. Family function: Order. Cost dimension: the standard that steadies; the frame that holds you holds you in. Arena: the gate, the seal, order, the appointed hour. Classical portrait: framework-mediated pressure; the standard that steadies; rank held by rules, rigidity as the shadow. Ruled domains: Career, Status, Order. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 七杀.
Element arena: Water (depth, current, tide, rain, spring, flow). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Fire. structural_interaction seed: "Water setting standard for Fire cross-polarity — depth asking whether warmth is sustainable".
- k2_overview: "Your Water moves as the Magistrate: navigable law, order that flows. You govern the way good rivers govern valleys, setting course without shouting, adjusting to terrain while staying a river. Your rules bend around cases and still arrive at the sea. It is the subtlest authority, and people obey it thinking they chose to."
- k2_functional: "Your order runs like a canal: dug once with care, then carrying everyone’s traffic for decades."
- adj_chips: {"catalyst":["Clockwork","Composed","Far-sighted"],"friction":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Career":"Your career advances by navigation: reading currents, timing passages, arriving at rank without visible strain. Diplomacy, coordination, the harbor-master roles. Your course is quiet and it compounds.","Status":"Your standing spreads like watershed reputation: carried by word of mouth into places you have never been. Tend the source. Everything downstream tastes of it.","Order":"Your order is current-shaped: rules that adapt to terrain yet keep direction. People experience your governance as ease. Document the channel, or it evaporates when you do."}

  - row 0: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 1: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 2: [REDACTED: the target row]
- Sibling cell 水_七杀 chips (nothing you write may fit the sibling): {"catalyst":["Cool-headed","Unblinking","Deep-striking"],"friction":["Chilling","Relentless","Suffocating"]}
- Sibling cell 水_七杀 friction row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Your displeasure arrives as temperature. There is never a scene: the warmth simply leaves the water, and everyone in it notices at once. People can handle anger. The cold is harder, because there is nothing to answer and nowhere to warm up."

Core element Fire, energy element Water. Law: Water tames Fire (水克火: rain ends the blaze). Relative to the core the energy is the tamer, so Water is this core's Order. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Fire core that shows Water on the friction pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The friction pole of Water as the Order is the Underfueled band's case (the core burns more than it takes in); tone by pole: reminder. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 火_水's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: You play safe before you know the odds. Keeping what you have feels more like you than reaching, so you take the safe way ahead of the good one. Remember that playing it safe has a price, and you pay it in chances never taken.

value_b.text: Playing it safe is your answer to anything new. Since a loss shows and a missed gain never does, you would rather play safe than risk your place. You stay right where you are on the safe choice, and that is the thing to remember.

value.text: For everyone waiting on your yes, you play it safe too. You would rather give a safe no than a yes that can fail, and the real answer stays yours. Do not forget that a safe answer leaves them waiting instead of deciding.

value.text: You wait for permission that is not coming. Being given permission feels safer than taking it, and you wait to be asked up rather than step up unasked. You hold most of the permission you wait for, a fact you keep forgetting.

value_b.text: Waiting for permission is how you earn a place. Since a place you were given feels safer than one you took, you wait to be chosen rather than step forward. Remember that you wait longest for the permission you never think to give yourself.

value.text: You bite your tongue long before anyone asks you to. You bite down rather than cost the mood, since a smooth evening feels safer to you than an honest one. You keep the peace by biting your tongue, and you alone carry what went unsaid.

value_b.text: Biting your tongue is your first move in a disagreement. Because your standing matters more to you than your point, you bite your tongue and keep your place. You will need that bitten tongue the day you must speak, and it is out of practice.

value.text: Safe and unheard is where biting your tongue leaves you. You would rather bite your tongue than put your standing on the line for a point. You hand away the credit for everything you bit back, and a point never made cannot be yours.

value.text: Your tongue gets bitten hardest around the people who need your answer. You keep things smooth instead of saying what you see, so you bite down while a bad plan passes. Biting your tongue costs them the one no they needed from you.
